title: Number to hexadecimal
description:
Write `toHex(value)`. It returns the hexadecimal digits of `value` as a string, in capitals, with no `0x` in front and no leading zeros.

`toHex(255)` is `"FF"`. `toHex(256)` is `"100"`. `toHex(0)` is `"0"`.

Produce the digits yourself. `std::hex`, `std::format` and `printf` are not allowed here.
hints: `value % 16` is a number from 0 to 15, which is exactly one hex digit: the last one. `value / 16` is what is left once that digit is removed.
To turn 0 to 15 into a character, index into a string of all sixteen digits: `"0123456789ABCDEF"[digit]`.
The digits come out last one first. Either put each new digit at the front of the string, or add them at the end and reverse the string when the loop finishes.
A loop that runs "while value is greater than 0" produces nothing at all for 0. Handle that case separately.
rules: Build the digits yourself, without a library formatter.
